title: Effect of Milk Scum biodiesel addition and hydrogen energy share on the performance of reactivity‐controlled compression ignition engine
content:
Abstract

Reactivity Controlled Compression Ignition (RCCI) engines are a promising way to decarbonize the internal combustion engine industry. Despite this extensive literature covering dual-fuel setups, a critical knowledge gap persists regarding the steady-state combustion behavior of highly specific, waste-derived oxygenated lipids when paired directly with carbon-free LRFs. To address this gap, the current study focuses on the waste-to-wealth principle of utilizing Milk Scum biodiesel and mineral diesel (as a High-Reactivity Fuel) and hydrogen (as an LRF) to achieve the minimum carbon-based emissions. Experimentally, performance and emissions were measured using a constant-rpm diesel engine with a compression ratio of 18, fuel injection pressure of 500 bar, fuel injection time of 23 bTDC, and common-rail direct-injected (B10, B15, and B20) and port-injected hydrogen (0.077 and 0.121 kg/h) at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% engine loads. The measurements indicate that the RCCI optimality (0.121 kg/h H2, B10 blend) achieved a maximum Brake Thermal Efficiency of 31.2% and 10–15% lower Brake Specific Fuel Consumption under high-load conditions. Moreover, this hydrogen-enriched RCCI mode achieved average reductions in CO, HC, NOx, and smoke emissions of 24%, 27%, 35%, and 40%, respectively. Interestingly, while the overall experimental matrix yielded an average NOx reduction of 35%, the optimum RCCI B10 configuration at 100% load inhibited peak NOx formation by more than 60% compared with the baseline diesel mode at the same load.
